details:
This package contains no JavaScript. It is a delivery vehicle for a Windows executable: NULLSUB.exe (1,300,309 bytes, x64 PE, package is win32-only), plus a second copy inside NULLSUB[.]zip, advertised as a "portable Windows activator for desktop AI apps" that the reader is told to download and double-click (the README points at hxxps://cdn[.]jsdelivr[.]net/npm/nullsub/NULLSUB[.]exe and hxxps://nullsub[.]ink). The binary is an encrypted-payload loader with active defence evasion, evidenced by its own strings and imports: - Hidden stage: "carrier=1 chunks=5", "[payload] %zu bytes", "[crypto] decrypted, magic=%02x%02x%02x%02x", "[crc] chunk %u mismatch" — a five-chunk encrypted blob decrypted at startup, then memory-mapped and executed by a bundled reflective PE loader ("[ldr] mapping %zu bytes", "[ldr] relocs ok", "[ldr].NET image, launch mode", "map failed (%d), temp fallback" → "[temp] launched %ls"). It also skips its own anti-sleep delay ("[sleep] skipped (fast start)").
- AV/EDR neutering: "[patch] %s!%s stomped" together with AmsiScanBuffer, AmsiScanString, AmsiOpenSession (amsi.dll) and EtwEventWrite, EtwEventWriteFull, EventWrite (ntdll.dll / advapi32.dll) — the process patches out AMSI scanning and ETW telemetry before running the payload.
- Privilege escalation: if not elevated it hijacks "Software\Classes\ms-settings\Shell\Open\command" with DelegateExecute and falls back to computerdefaults.exe / fodhelper.exe ("[uac] not elevated, hijacking ms-settings", "computerdefaults failed … trying fodhelper", "[uac] cleaned").
- Analysis evasion and host fingerprinting: CPUID hypervisor checks, IsDebuggerPresent / CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, process enumeration via CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, GetAdaptersAddresses (MAC/adapters), GetVolumeInformationW, GetSystemFirmwareTable and GlobalMemoryStatusEx, plus a check for loaded drivers under \drivers\.
- Imports include CreateProcessW, VirtualAlloc, VirtualProtect, WriteFile and RegSetValueExW. No command-and-control hostname or IP is present in the binary; the second stage exists only in encrypted form, so its network indicators are not observable from the package itself.
